resolutions.researcher_notes: This batch's KNOWN GOTCHA applies: the live opec.org ASB2012 link (per seed_citations) is dead (redirects to homepage; url_verifier returns 200-but-missing-token because the PDF's text stream is compressed and the naive substring check can't reach it). Recovered via Wayback (https://web.archive.org/web/20120722013100/.../ASB2012.pdf, CDX-confirmed live capture) and manually ran `pdftotext -layout` -> Table 4.10 'Gas pipelines in OPEC Members, 2011', Libya section, p.75, exact row: 'Bouri/Bahr Assalam | Mellitah Oil and Gas | 20 [mi] | 10 [in] | 3,879,921 [1,000 scm/yr] | na'. This is a specific named match for this exact pipeline, listed as extant transport infrastructure in 2011 (not proposed/planned) -- supports Status=operating. Second, independently-recovered OPEC snapshot (ASB2017, Wayback https://web.archive.org/web/20231204014748/.../ASB2017_13062017.pdf, manually pdftotext'd, Table 9.9 'Main gas pipelines in OPEC Members, 2016', p.133-134) still lists 'Bouri offshore/Bahr Es Salam (2) | Mellitha Oil & Gas | 2 x 12 [mi] | 4, 10 [in]' -- confirms the route was still active 5 years later (2016 data), now apparently with a second parallel line added (4in) alongside the original 10in line. Third, independent (non-OPEC) source: Mellitah's own corporate 'About the Company' page (mellitahog.ly, Arabic, verified live) states Mellitah Oil & Gas operates both the Bouri field (130km north of Tripoli) and the Bahr Essalam field (110km northwest of Tripoli), i.e. confirms the company is currently, actively running both endpoints of this corridor. Three origins (OPEC statistical body across two editions, and Mellitah's own site) -- tier high. Note: ASB2017's length figure for the 10in line (12 mi) differs from ASB2012's (20 mi) for the same route -- see Length unit notes for this discrepancy; it does not affect the Status determination.

Fuel=Gas is definitional to the recovered OPEC ASB2012 table this row sits in ('Gas pipelines in OPEC Members, 2011', Table 4.10, p.75 -- as opposed to Table 4.11, the parallel petroleum-products-pipeline table a few pages later, which lists a different Libya roster) -- see Status notes for the Wayback recovery/pdftotext method. Independent corroboration: the Wikipedia 'Greenstream' pipeline article (verified live, contains both 'Bouri' and 'Bahr Essalam') states the Bahr Essalam offshore field, Bouri Field, and Wafa field all feed gas into the Mellitah complex/compressor station that supplies the Greenstream export line to Sicily -- consistent with a gas (not oil) pipeline linking Bouri to Bahr Essalam/Mellitah. Two independent origins (OPEC statistical body vs. a general encyclopedia entry on the export pipeline this corridor feeds) -- tier medium given neither source is pipeline-specific/dedicated on fuel type alone.

Recovered Wayback ASB2012 (see Status notes), Table 4.10, Libya, 'Bouri/Bahr Assalam | Mellitah Oil and Gas' row: Capacity column = 3,879,921 (units: 1,000 scm/yr per the table's column header) = 3,879,921,000 scm/yr = 3.879921 bcm/y -- an exact match (to 3 significant figures) to the sheet's value ('3.88' bcm/y). This precision is strong evidence this is the sheet's original source data point. The later ASB2017 recapture of the same route (Table 9.9, 2016 data) dropped the capacity/amount-transported columns entirely (that edition's table only reports length and diameter), so no second numeric capacity figure was available there to corroborate or contradict. Web search budget was exhausted this session before an exhaustive check for a non-OPEC capacity figure (e.g. an Eni/Mellitah technical factsheet) could be completed. Single source; tier medium.

CONTRADICTION TO FLAG: Recovered Wayback ASB2012, Table 4.10, Libya, 'Bouri/Bahr Assalam' row gives Length = 20 miles = 32.19 km (20 x 1.609344), which is a close match to the sheet's LengthKnown value of 32.00 km (~0.6% / ~0.2km apart) -- clearly the same table row given the exact-match Diameter (10in) and Capacity (3,879,921) also line up (see those units), so I'm confident this is GEM's original source. However, the later OPEC ASB2017 recapture of the same route (Table 9.9, 2016 data, manually pdftotext'd) gives a materially different figure: 'Bouri offshore/Bahr Es Salam (2) | Mellitha Oil & Gas | 2 x 12 [mi] | 4, 10 [in]' -- i.e. by 2016 OPEC records TWO parallel lines of 12 miles (19.3km) each, diameters 4in and 10in, rather than one 20-mile 10in line. This could mean: (a) a second, smaller-diameter line was added between 2011 and 2016 alongside the original, and/or (b) the route was re-surveyed/re-measured (12mi vs 20mi is a large, non-trivial change, not a rounding artifact). Since the sheet's row is specifically the 10in line (matching Diameter exactly) and its length (32.00km) tracks the 2012 figure far better than the 2016 one, I'm citing ASB2012 as the primary support and flagging the ASB2017 discrepancy rather than citing it as corroboration (it would actually contradict, not confirm, the sheet's length value) or fabricating an explanation. tier low given this unresolved cross-edition conflict on length specifically (Diameter and Capacity are not affected by it).

Recovered Wayback ASB2012, Table 4.10, Libya, 'Bouri/Bahr Assalam' row: Diameter column = 10 (inches) -- exact match to the sheet's value ('10.00', DiameterUnits='in'). Corroborated by the later Wayback ASB2017 recapture (Table 9.9, 2016 data), which lists the same corridor ('Bouri offshore/Bahr Es Salam') with diameters '4, 10' (in) for its two parallel lines -- the 10in figure persists across both editions, consistent with the sheet's single tracked 'Pipeline 1' segment being this 10in line (the 4in line appears to be a separate, untracked segment). Both citations are the same origin (OPEC), five years apart, so counted as independent=false rather than two genuinely separate sources; no non-OPEC source found stating this specific pipeline's diameter. tier medium.

Country-level value only (Start/EndCountryOrArea = Libya, both ends unnamed at the sub-national level in the brief -- reasonable since this is an offshore field-to-field line, not a route with named onshore towns). Three independent sources agree: (1) recovered Wayback ASB2012 Table 4.10 lists this row under the 'Libya' section heading. (2) Mellitah's own corporate site (mellitahog.ly, verified live) states the Bouri field sits '130km north of Tripoli' and the Bahr Essalam field '110km northwest of Tripoli' -- both plainly within Libyan territorial/offshore jurisdiction. (3) offshore-technology.com's Bouri field profile (verified live) describes it as 'offshore the Libyan coast, in the Mediterranean Sea', within Block NC-41. Three genuinely independent origins (an intergovernmental statistics body, the operating company, and an industry trade profile) -- tier high, though the underlying claim (country=Libya) is not in serious doubt for an intra-Libyan-waters field-to-field pipeline.

Operator='Mellitah Oil & Gas' confirmed by three independent origins: (1) recovered Wayback ASB2012 Table 4.10 names 'Mellitah Oil and Gas' as owner/operator of the exact 'Bouri/Bahr Assalam' row. (2) Mellitah's own corporate 'About the Company' page (mellitahog.ly, Arabic, verified live) confirms the company operates both the Bouri and Bahr Essalam fields, and gives the Arabic company name matching the sheet's OperatorLocalLanguage field ('مليته للنفط و الغاز بي في'). (3) NOC's own official affiliated-companies page (noc.ly, verified live) lists 'Mellitah Oil & Gas' (Arabic: شركة مليته للنفط والغاز بي.في) as one of NOC's subsidiary/affiliated companies -- independently corroborates both the Operator and OperatorLocalLanguage values from the state oil company's own site. Three genuinely independent origins (an intergovernmental statistics body, the operating company itself, and its state-owned parent) -- tier high.

Could not verify the specific ownership split stated in the brief (Owner1=Libyan National Oil Corp 50.00%, Owner2=Eni SpA 50.00%). CONTRADICTION TO FLAG: offshore-technology.com's Bouri field profile (verified live) states the Bouri field/Block NC-41 concession is held 70% National Oil Corporation / 30% ENI, with the two partners jointly establishing Mellitah Oil and Gas Company to manage operations -- i.e. a genuinely different split (70/30, not 50/50) from the sheet's value, at least at the underlying concession level. It is plausible the sheet's 50/50 figure instead describes the Mellitah Oil & Gas B.V. joint-venture *company* structure itself (commonly reported elsewhere as an equal NOC-Eni JV) rather than the Bouri concession's equity, but I found no source -- Eni's own site (returned 404 on the Libya operations pages I tried), NOC's site, Wikipedia (no dedicated Mellitah Oil & Gas or Western Libya Gas Project article exists), or trade press -- that states a 50/50 split specifically for this pipeline or its operating JV. WebSearch tool budget was exhausted this session (200/200 calls used) before a broader search (e.g. an Eni annual report/20-F-equivalent disclosure, or a Wood Mackenzie/Rystad-style JV factsheet) could be run to resolve the discrepancy. Per standing rule 2 (never fabricate) and given the one source found actually conflicts with the sheet's value rather than supporting it, leaving this UNRESOLVED rather than citing a contradicting or unconfirmed source -- flagging for a future pass with search budget to check Eni's annual report/investor disclosures for the Mellitah Oil & Gas B.V. JV equity split specifically (as distinct from the NC-41/Bouri concession split, which appears to be 70/30 NOC/Eni per offshore-technology.com).
